title: Retention Governor for Multi-Tenant Request Artifacts and Evidence Scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers need deterministic, auditable retention behavior across prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics while operating in multi-tenant environments with mixed residency and legal holds. Current TTL plumbing enforces deletion dates but offers limited preflight validation, lacks a scheduled evidence-export cadence, and provides no automatic conflict resolution for overlapping per-tenant and global policies.

Goal: Deliver a Retention Governor service + Console UI that validates retention policy sets, computes effective per-route/tenant TTLs, schedules bundled evidence exports (attested bundles with hashes), and orchestrates safe evictions/backfills with configurable grace windows. The Governor should support dry-run validation, SLA-aware eviction throttling, and a recoverable delete pipeline that preserves forensic evidence when requested.

Scope: PM, Console UX, API schema changes, retention-executor orchestration, evidence-bundling service, and integration tests. Out of scope: full legal review workflows and long-term archival storage—those are separate infra projects.
acceptance_criteria:
- Console: 'Retention Governor' UI surface that shows computed effective TTL per tenant/route, inheritance tree, and a dry-run validator.
- API: POST /retention/validate that returns policy conflicts, effective TTL map, and suggested fixes.
- Scheduler: Configurable evidence-export cadence (daily/weekly/monthly) per tenant with attested bundle generation and hash chain metadata.
- Safe eviction: Eviction jobs must respect legal holds and grace windows; deleted artifacts are recorded in an audit manifest for 90 days before physical purge.
- Observability: Per-tenant eviction metrics, export success/failure, and a Console timeline view for recent retention operations.
- Tests: End-to-end test covering policy inheritance, conflict resolution, and dry-run correctness for 3 tenant profiles.
- Security: KMS-backed signing of evidence bundles and RBAC checks for scheduling/exporting actions.
implementation_notes: Design a compact retention policy DSL that supports: default/global, tenant-level override, route-level override, and conditional legal-hold tags.
Reuse ENG-51234 runtime-config hooks for applying TTL at request ingestion; add a validation layer that can run independently of runtime enforcement.
Scheduler will emit export tasks into the evidence-bundler service; bundler signs bundles with KMS and uploads to an S3-compatible store with expirable links.
Eviction pipeline: mark-for-eviction -> attach audit manifest -> start background purge after grace window. Provide an emergency-recovery path to rehydrate recent artifacts within 72 hours.
Provide a 'dry-run' endpoint in the Console that accepts a policy set and a tenant sample and returns a human-readable diff of what would change.
Rate-limit backfills/evictions per-tenant to preserve runtime SLOs; integrate with Dedicated capacity autoscaler for large bulk operations.
Add a lightweight simulator in Console (subset of retention-simulator) focused on export cadence and artifact bundling size estimation.
Create migration steps for existing tenants: 1) compute effective TTLs, 2) notify affected teams via email/webhook, 3) schedule staggered evictions to avoid resource spikes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): Internal-only for compliance and SRE teams. Validate dry-run and bundle signing. Expect 2-week alpha window.
Phase 2 (beta): Invite 3 pilot tenants (one small, one mid, one enterprise) to opt in. Monitor export times and eviction impact on SLOs for 4 weeks.
Phase 3 (general): Gradual enable by tenant with feature flag. Provide migration tooling and 30-day notice for tenants with manual overrides.
Rollback: If export failures exceed threshold or eviction jobs cause >1% latency regression, pause Governor and revert to existing TTL enforcement.
Comms: Publish runbook, release notes, and a sample Confluence policy library for common compliance profiles.
Support: Solutions engineering to run tenant onboarding sessions and run the first 5 evidence exports as assisted operations.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Large parallel evictions could spike storage I/O and affect serving latency. Mitigation: strict per-tenant rate limits and staged backfill windows tied to Dedicated autoscaling.

Risk: Misconfigured policies accidentally purge data. Mitigation: require two-step approval for any policy that reduces effective TTL by >30% and implement mandatory dry-run with signed acceptance for enterprise tenants.
Risk: Evidence bundle integrity concerns. Mitigation: sign bundles with KMS, attach per-bundle hash chain, and provide a bundle-verifier tool for customers.
Risk: Regulatory/legal holds not honored. Mitigation: integrate with legal-hold tagging; legal-hold tags override evictions and are surfaced prominently in the Console with an immutable flag.
